title: The Fall of Koel and the Opening of the Ghallughara

blocks.text: This page closes the Mathura and Koel episode by showing how the fall of those centers shook Jat power and widened Abdali's authority after Panipat. With Agra and surrounding positions subdued, the narrative briefly surveys his larger settlement of north Indian affairs through appointments and renewed control in places such as Delhi, Sirhind, Lahore, and Amritsar.

That wider frame is important because it shows the Afghan ruler turning from one set of enemies to another while the subcontinent still trembles from recent war. The mention of three lakh horse-mounted soldiers from the South and the redistribution of authority under Najib Khan underline the scale of imperial reordering now underway.

The page then pivots directly toward Sikh history with the explicit signal, Now as came the turn of the Sikhs. In doing so it opens Episode 136 and prepares the reader for the Ghallughara near Malerkotla, where Abdali's reorganized power will collide with the Khalsa in a far more tragic campaign.
